title: Router trace-gap led to variant mistag and cascading retries — remediation plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: After a regional capacity surge on 2026-03-03 we observed a spike of 5xxs and elevated latencies in the hosted API. Root cause analysis shows a gap in request-trace propagation between the edge routing layer and the policy evaluation service, which allowed stale policy/variant-tag state to be applied. The stale tags caused an incompatible model variant to be selected for a subset of requests, which in turn triggered repeated fallback attempts and a short-lived cross-region retry spiral. This ticket tracks the remediation, validation, and long-term hardening work.
timeline: 2026-03-03 09:12 UTC: Automated alert - increase in 5xx rate from us-west-2 cluster; latency p95 rose from 180ms to 420ms.
2026-03-03 09:18 UTC: Engineering on-call identified elevated fallback rates and cross-region retries for customers on heavy chat workloads.
2026-03-03 09:35 UTC: Identified mismatch between routing decision traces and policy evaluation logs; trace IDs missing in policy-service for ~4% of requests during surge.
2026-03-03 10:05 UTC: Temporary mitigation - tightened client retry window and added emergency BGP weight change to shift traffic away from most impacted nodes.
2026-03-04 11:00 UTC: Post-incident RCA kickoff; assembled cross-team group (runtime, routing, gateway, telemetry).
root_cause: A trace-propagation regression in the gateway introduced intermittent loss of X-Route-Trace header when the gateway was under heavy backpressure. The policy service uses the trace header to look up recently computed variant-tag and policy decisions; when missing, it fell back to an eventual-consistency cache that contained stale variant tags. Those stale tags pointed to an incompatible quantized model variant for certain request sequences, leading to token-level failures and repeated fallback attempts which triggered cross-region retries.
impact: Brief (~40m) customer-visible increase in 5xx errors for hosted API; affected heavy streaming chat workloads and mid-tier customers in US-WEST-2 and fallbacked into EU region creating higher cross-region costs and degraded latency. Estimated 1.2% increase in token error rate for impacted customers during the window.
metrics: Fallback attempts per request (median) increased from 1 to 3 during surge
action_items: RTG-1: Add end-to-end propagation test for X-Route-Trace across gateway -> routing -> policy-service (owner: Marco Jensen, estimate: 2)
RTG-2: Make policy-service treat missing trace header as 'fail open' with conservative variant selection rather than reading eventual cache (owner: Lina Gomez, estimate: 3)
RTG-3: Invalidate variant cache on model-signature-change events and add TTL shrink under high-backpressure conditions (owner: Samuel Ortiz, estimate: 5)
RTG-4: Add rate-limiter and exponential backoff in router when fallback-rate exceeds threshold to prevent cross-region retry spirals (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 3)
RTG-5: Deploy a lightweight canary that simulates header-loss and validates system-wide behavior before full rollout (owner: Marco Jensen, estimate: 2)
RTG-6: Update runbook to include explicit steps for isolating stale-policy-cache issues and emergency mitigation checklist (owner: On-call team, estimate: 1)
RTG-7: Post-deploy monitoring dashboard tile for 'trace-propagation-loss' with alerts at 0.5% of requests missing route-trace header (owner: Observability team, estimate: 2)
RTG-8: Audit recent gateway changes and revert trace header optimization that introduced regression if test fails (owner: Gateway team, estimate: 1)
RTG-9: Customer follow-up: targeted message to impacted customers describing root cause and compensatory measures (owner: Customer Success, estimate: 1)
RTG-10: Add CI job injecting backpressure to gateway tests to catch header-drop regressions in pre-prod (owner: QA, estimate: 3)
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Initial mitigation validated; emergency BGP weight change rolled back after traffic stabilized.
2026-03-07: Marco opened PR #1426 in routing-service to add end-to-end trace checks (https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1426).
2026-03-09: Policy-service change candidate implementing conservative missing-trace handling submitted for review (https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy/pull/783).
2026-03-11: Observability added dashboard prototype for trace-loss; alert thresholds discussed and approved by SRE.
2026-03-13: Canary plan drafted and scheduled for 2026-03-17 in us-west-2 with 1% traffic window.
2026-03-14: Gatekeeper review completed for RTG-2; security review not required for code changes but ops playbook update required.
decisions: Do not restore previous gateway optimization that elided trace headers until canary and CI tests are in place.
Policy-service will prefer a conservative default variant (older, broadly compatible) when request trace is missing, rather than consulting eventual cache.
Introduce circuit-breaker on router fallback rate to stop cascading retries between regions.
Run targeted customer communications for impacted accounts once mitigations are deployed and validated.
tests: E2E: Simulate trace header loss in pre-prod and validate policy-service and router fallbacks behave as expected.
Load: Apply synthetic backpressure on gateway to reproduce header-drop scenario and ensure CI catches regression.
CHAOS: Small-scale chaos experiment to randomly drop X-Route-Trace across control plane and monitor for cross-region retry amplification.
Integration: Verify variant-cache invalidation on model-signature change events across all regions.
rollout_plan: Staged rollout: merge fixes to routing and policy services -> deploy to staging -> run E2E header-loss canaries -> deploy to us-west-2 1% -> 10% -> global. Monitor fallback rate, 5xx, and cross-region egress cost metrics at each step. Hold rollback window of 30 minutes at each stage.
postmortem_notes: This event highlights a systemic coupling between routing trace propagation and policy cache correctness. Short-term mitigation focused on conservative fallback and emergency traffic steering; long-term must prioritize trace-safety guarantees and defensive defaults. The team recommends a small framework-level contract for essential headers that must be preserved under backpressure and irreversible router changes.
